raw.title: P3: 30–50 evidence-grounded Self-Instruct candidate seed pilot
raw.body:
## Corrected objective
P3 produces candidate **LLM diagnostic interpretation and experience-reuse** SFT examples. It does not ask the LLM to diagnose raw telemetry.

LLM input must be a structured case packet containing:
- upstream ML/statistical diagnosis results (method/version, analysis scope, candidate findings, scores with semantics/calibration status, evidence IDs and limitations);
- diagnostic logs (alarms, events, operator notes, engineering analysis, maintenance and prior disposition);
- spacecraft configuration and subsystem/component context;
- mission phase, operating mode, recent operations and constraints;
- relevant historical cases with confirmed/unresolved/rejected outcomes and transfer limitations;
- reviewed domain passages / knowledge evidence.

Raw telemetry remains with upstream ML methods. At most, retain a restricted artifact reference for provenance; do not inline waveforms or high-rate time series in LLM prompts.

## New contracts
- `resources/diagnostic_case.schema.json`: case packet + expected reviewed report.
- `resources/diagnostic_sft.schema.json`: chat-style SFT export.
- `examples/diagnostic_context_case_illustrative.json`: hypothetical illustration only.
- `docs/DATASET_PURPOSE_CORRECTION.md`: responsibilities, task families and acceptance criteria.

## Entry sequence
1. D0 inventory existing diagnostic reports, ML result bundles, logs, context, historical cases and expert-reviewed outcomes.
2. Build 20 manually curated schema-valid cases to verify task coverage and evidence lineage.
3. Only if approved cases support it, proceed to a 300–500 example controlled SFT pilot.

R4 may add upstream ML evidence and additional diagnostic episodes, but it is not a prerequisite if existing reviewed diagnosis-result/context packets suffice.

## Task families
- diagnostic_synthesis
- historical_case_reuse
- conflict_reconciliation
- evidence_sufficiency
- next_step_recommendation
- handover_summary

## Acceptance
- [ ] Input includes machine diagnosis result and context, not raw telemetry.
- [ ] The target interprets upstream ML outputs without silently re-running or overruling the detector.
- [ ] ML scores retain semantics and calibration status; never treat an uncalibrated score as probability.
- [ ] Fault-source component and affected components are represented separately.
- [ ] Historical unresolved cases remain unresolved precedents.
- [ ] Claims cite log/result/history/knowledge evidence references.
- [ ] Conflicts, missing context, uncertainty and abstention are explicitly represented.
- [ ] Human approval, source-group provenance and episode-level split are mandatory before Gold/SFT export.

Fine-tuning evaluation compares base LLM, ordinary Self-Instruct SFT and DGSI context-grounded SFT on identical held-out diagnosis-context packets. The target metric is second-stage interpretation and report quality, not raw-telemetry detector accuracy.

### 2026-11-15 — PR #27 standalone SFT provenance gate
- [Draft PR #27](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/27) blocks invented, omitted or duplicated log/passage refs and an absent spacecraft context anchor in direct SFT validation; lineage batch checks inherit it. Case→SFT error compatibility preserved.
- [Ubuntu + Windows successful CI](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43677727204), 322 tests per platform, 12 new SYNTHETIC-only adversarial methods.
- Does not prove evidence authenticity or source permission; structural passes remain `gold_eligible=false`. No real Gold created.
- Keep task families and upstream-ML/LLM boundary unchanged; next highest-value action is authorized 5–10-case expert adjudication, then 20-case curated SFT pilot only when evidence complete. No raw telemetry or R21 material in the public repository.


### 2026-11-15 P3 evidence and pilot boundary
- [Draft PR #30](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/30) adds manifest-to-Case alignment and synthetic-to-real laundering regression; [CI 43686403514](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43686403514): Ubuntu + Windows **369 tests each PASS**, 17 new SYNTHETIC adversarial methods.
- Evidence consistency, structural validity, file declarations and permission assertions **do not constitute expert adjudication or Gold**. The author can still forge matching metadata; independent authorized source verification is mandatory.
- Keep the product goal solely SFT for ML-result/log/context/history **second-stage diagnostic reasoning**. Raw telemetry is upstream-only.
- Maintain the sequence: 5–10 independently expert-audited de-identified real episodes → 20 curated high-quality samples → only on verified source density and quality, controlled 300–500 sample pilot. Current newly verified real Gold count: **0**; TC01–TC09 are SYNTHETIC_TEST_ONLY.
- No source upload, main merge, fine-tune, train split or automatic Gold promotion.


### 2026-11-15 — L0 review intake and source-migration controls
- The returned audit package confirms that the five user source cases remain source-attribution L0 material, not independently verified root-cause targets.
- Public literature now distinguishes flight events, ground tests and knowledge-only sources. The ISEE/IUE expert-system demonstration is excluded from incident counts.
- TROPICS payload A/B outcomes are split into distinct episodes within one event family, preventing outcome collapse during split construction.
- NASA TM-100232 report year and NTRS accession year are separate metadata fields.
- No reviewed L0 card is promoted to Gold. Complete LLM-facing SFT still requires upstream ML results, diagnostic logs, mission/configuration context, historical evidence provenance and an independently adjudicated target.


### Final verification — 2026-11-15
- PR #35 latest head: `7c5a969048b7f7b09dcc1300dc1477769e9529fd`.
- [Push CI 43721453245](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43721453245): Ubuntu PASS, Windows PASS.
- [PR CI 43721448889](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43721448889): Ubuntu PASS, Windows PASS.
- 12 public-literature L0 cards are now in the PR branch. TROPICS A/B outcomes are separate episodes; NASA 22N injector/catalyst findings and Lunar Orbiter observations remain distinct episodes within their source families.
- L0 cards remain not SFT eligible. No Gold, model training or main-branch merge.


### 2026-11-15 — P4 independent L1 coverage and blinded-review metadata gate (Draft PR #42)
- [x] Added metadata-only L1 portfolio coverage: six task families, historical Context status buckets, event-family counts, and separate real-candidate versus literature-derived synthetic counts. No source case identifiers or diagnostic text in audit output.
- [x] Blocks formal split assignments on unreviewed collections and duplicate task IDs across collections.
- [x] Added dual anonymous review-scorecard validator for seven engineering dimensions (1–5), fixed finding codes, independent reviewer tokens and automatic secure-adjudication flag on disagreement. This cannot verify reviewer identity or approve Gold/training.
- [x] Added 12 SYNTHETIC_TEST_ONLY adversarial tests and [coverage/blind review rubric](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/blob/feat/l1-coverage-blind-review-20261115/docs/L1_TASK_COVERAGE_AND_BLIND_REVIEW.md).
- [x] Draft [PR #42](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/42), based on PR #40, exact head `2ee78727c0d6a5100a780b6b3d4507ab75f75d42`. [PR CI run 43727595149](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43727595149): Ubuntu **555/555 PASS**, Windows **555/555 PASS**.
- Baseline: 3 L1 SYNTHETIC task packets / 3 distinct source event families / 2 diagnostic_synthesis + 1 conflict_reconciliation / 0 real Gold / 0 assigned splits. Other four task families still need coverage.
- PR #41 independently adds historical applicability and a nine-dimension expert quality rubric; reconcile the two review layers before adoption to avoid competing approval semantics. Neither PR is merged.
- Expert review is pending for first 3 L1 tasks and source cards. No training, Gold promotion or private data upload.

# Authoritative migration decision — 2026-11-03

**New source of truth:** `interplanetarysister/interplanetary-fund2@main` is the canonical **frontend, interaction, asset, and functional reference** (original Base44-era APK experience). It is NOT the target production runtime. `interplanetarysister/InterplanetaryFund` remains the deployable migration repository, hosted on Cloudflare Pages/Workers with Supabase. Preserve all working migration code; no Convex or Vercel.

## Implementation order
1. Inventory original pages, assets, routes, UI flows, AI wizard, backend SDK calls, and feature flags from interplanetary-fund2 main. Inventory existing migrated features and PRs in InterplanetaryFund. Produce a feature-to-backend replacement matrix.
2. Import/adapt the original frontend and space/cyberpunk mobile-first design into a dedicated migration branch of InterplanetaryFund; retain functionality, images, page names, campaign discovery, globe, and five-choice campaign AI flow. Generate five title choices, two short-description choices, one story at a time with section regeneration, and optional themed AI artwork. Preserve prior improvements where compatible.
3. Replace **every** Base44 dependency systematically, including hidden SDK calls, auth, entities, functions, agents, storage, AI, campaigns, payments, webhooks, and workflows, with Cloudflare Workers and Supabase adapters. Do not leave production runtime dependent on Base44. No mock payments. Preserve 7% withdrawal fee and owner-only financial controls.
4. Allow guest browsing and draft campaign composition; require login only when posting/saving, then return to draft. Repair password sign-in, password recovery, and admin access safely. Verify account mapping and RLS.
5. Build from the correct migrated frontend directory and deploy to a true preview URL; check actual rendered page parity, mobile usability, assets, API responses, auth, draft recovery, and no redirect loops. Compare against original APK/ZIP and 59-route matrix; reconcile backend entrypoints.
6. Merge reviewed, passing changes to main and promote to production only after explicit end-to-end verification. Preserve Cloudflare domain fixes, SSL, dedicated API/workflow routes, Supabase production and legacy data, secrets, and rollback. Do not retire Base44 until parity is proven.

## Current verified deployment hazard
Cloudflare Pages project interplanetaryfund-migration is GitHub-connected to InterplanetaryFund/main. Its current configuration root_dir is apps/web but canonical production deployment 321ccced (2026-11-03 13:08 UTC, commit 68bcbb4) built from root /; production_deployments_enabled=false. Preview deployments are mixed idle/success/failure. Do not treat a 200 HTTP status as frontend parity. Restore and verify build provenance before production promotion.

**Acceptance:** The original app's frontend is visually and functionally preserved, with all Base44 services migrated to Cloudflare/Supabase, mobile-first, guest access, functional login, successful preview, no redirect loops, and no regressions.

Phase 4 shipped the `payments` module (E07, #106). The owner then compared the running application with the mockup and found it short "in every area" (D-031). The audit of 2026-11-14 (`main` at `a312199`, code read) confirmed for payments:
- a rental creates no charge: `payments/di.ts` registers nothing under `payments.chargeService`, so the calls in `facilities/commands/rentals.ts` and `facilities/commands/requests.ts` do nothing;
- "Accept cash" opens on B-21 only, while the mockup opens the one cash form from B-21, B-22, B-29, the B-32 order rows and the dashboard;
- B-32 has no row actions, no "Ordered by" column, no supplier and no guardians of children without an order;
- refunds are API-only, a charge without a payer can never get one, there is no manual charge and a bank import cannot be deleted;
- no payments job runs by itself: charge generation, overdue reminders, the checkout sweep and campaign closing need an operator;
- M-08 starts with nothing ticked, refuses a partially paid charge and tells a guardian who is not the payer "Everything is paid"; M-15 … M-19 are thinner than the mockup;
- nobody on the club's side can tell whether Stripe is connected, and the checkout offers card only.

The base spec also names the treasurer as the actor although D-030 holds the role back (#245), and names two endpoints two ways. This epic files the payments parity spec's twelve phases as stories.

Who has it: the club administrator (who does the treasurer's work, D-030); guardians and adult participants as payers; coaches and coordinators; the facility attendant and renters, through the rental charge.

## 📋 Scope

Expected outcome: every payments function the mockup shows is reachable on the same screen, and no payments job needs an operator's command. J-C01 … J-C06 work, and a second audit pass over the screens in the spec's *Sources* finds no row marked GAP.

Out of scope:
- the treasurer role, its panel and the B-33 cash custody page (#245, #118: referenced, not re-created); until #118 lands a coach's cash stays under "Cash with you";
- the bottom bar's Payments tab, the "More" entries and the sidebar count badges (E09, navigation spec);
- the facilities side of the rental charge: payee, description, confirmation when paid, the report's payments figure (E11-S11);
- a group move within a period, a ward turning 18 and a payer who leaves (E13);
- renames (the navigation spec's glossary, D-031 §2);
- editing a charge (cancel and create again, DD-C12); sales documents; gateways other than Stripe; a `ProgressJob`; Stripe keys in a Vereino screen (DD-C11).

## ✅ Done when

- every story below is closed;
- AC-C01 … AC-C14 hold;
- the member pages (M-08, M-15 … M-19, the Today tiles) are checked at 375 px, in both locales, light and dark (D-029); the panel pages in both locales and both modes.

## 📝 Spec

Design authority: `.ai/specs/2026-11-14-vereino-parity-payments.md` (**Draft**, phases 1–12). It is an addendum to `.ai/specs/2026-10-27-vereino-club-payments.md` (phase 4: it completes REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-030 … REQ-033 and supersedes the rows listed in its header) and delivers the provider side of DD-19 of `.ai/specs/2026-10-27-vereino-facilities.md` (D-028).

Screens: `docs/ux-concept/README.md` B-01, B-10, B-20 … B-22, B-29 … B-32, M-08, M-15 … M-19; mockup `docs/ux-concept/mockups/app.ts` (`screenCharges`, `screenCharge`, `screenBank`, `cashForm`, `screenKitCampaignAdmin`, `screenKitBuilder`, `kitDashboardWidget`, `screenPerson`, `screenPayments`, `screenKitList`, `kitOrderPage`, `screenKitToken`, `screenCashMobile`, `screenGroupPayments`, `kitTodayTiles`, `rentalCharge`).

## ⚠️ Open questions

- **Blocking — readiness:** the spec is **Draft**. No story is ready until the owner reviews it, confirms its autonomous defaults (Q-C01 … Q-C16) and approves the items below (SDLC.md Definition of Ready).
- **Blocking — Q-C20, migrations:** migration A (`payments_charges` payer and payee institution, encrypted `payer_label`, two indexes; E12-S01), migration B (reminder markers and three settings switches; E12-S11), migration C (`payments_settings.online_methods`; E12-S12). Proposed default: approve as listed, each migration's SQL shown before it is applied.
- **Blocking — Q-C20, contracts:** Contract 1 (`payments.chargeService` registered with `payerDisplayName` and `statusOf`; E12-S01), Contract 2 (the checkout accepts `partially_paid`; E12-S08), Contract 3 (the charges list's default sort; E12-S02), Contract 4 (automatic generation and reminders on by default, guardianships assign payers; E12-S05, E12-S11), Contract 5 (new routes, commands, events, spot, schedules and error codes become protected surfaces; E12-S01, E12-S04, E12-S05, E12-S11). Same proposed default.
- **Non-blocking — Q-C22:** may the administrator record a refund made in the Stripe Dashboard after the gateway refused a late capture? Default: yes, as a reversing entry with a required reason.
- **Non-blocking — V-C01** (E12-S12; fallback: status "not verified") and **V-C02** (E12-S05; fallback: the daily generation also assigns payers).
- **Non-blocking — not covered by the spec:** the groups parity spec (A, risk table and V-A01) hands "`payments` reacts to `groups.membership.deleted`" to this spec, which has no requirement for it. The owner decides whether it belongs here; until then the groups confirm text warns that issued charges stay.

## 📋 Decisions in play

- D-029 — every role except the administrator works from the phone (AC-C10 … AC-C12 at 375 px)
- D-030 §2 — the club administrator does the treasurer's work; the treasurer role and B-33 stay held back (#245, #118); Q-049 and Q-050 confirmed
- D-031 §1 — the mockup is the model for layout (perspective order, B-32 columns, phone pages)
- D-031 §2 — names follow the mockup (the navigation spec's glossary)
- D-028 — `facilities` does not require `payments`; the rental charge is optional; letter-prefixed ids
- Facilities DD-19 — a rental and its charge commit or fail together (amended additively by Contract 1)
- Base spec DD-42 — the checkout sweep, overpayments and refunds through the gateway
- #118 — B-33 for the administrator only; #245 — the treasurer role, held back

## 📋 Stories
<!-- om-backlog: checklist, rewritten on every run -->
- [ ] #291 E12-S01 — A rental creates its charge payable to the facility owner, and the administrator finds it under "Rentals (municipality)"
- [ ] #292 E12-S02 — An administrator accepts cash from the charges list, a charge and the bank statement page, and B-21 and B-22 match the mockup
- [ ] #293 E12-S03 — An administrator runs a kit campaign from its record: who ordered, what is paid, cash and handover in the row
- [ ] #294 E12-S04 — An administrator decides each transfer with one button in the row and deletes an import from which nothing was booked
- [ ] #295 E12-S05 — An administrator adds a charge by hand, assigns a payer to a charge without one and sees a person's charges on their record
- [ ] #296 E12-S06 — An administrator refunds an online payment from the charge and finds every overpayment under "To refund"
- [ ] #297 E12-S07 — An administrator sees bank statements and cash, order campaigns and charges without a payer on the dashboard
- [ ] #298 E12-S08 — A payer pays everything on the phone in two taps, including what remains of a partly paid charge, and a guardian who is not the payer sees who pays
- [ ] #299 E12-S09 — A guardian follows a kit order on the phone: stage, deadlines, pickup and who handed it over
- [ ] #300 E12-S10 — The cash and coach pages name the receiver, list today's receipts, state the club's coach mode and show when a kit was handed over
- [ ] #301 E12-S11 — Charges are generated, overdue payers reminded, checkouts reconciled and campaigns closed on a schedule
- [ ] #302 E12-S12 — An administrator sees whether online payment is connected and chooses the payment methods offered to payers

raw.body:
## 2026-11-15 update — formal conclusion contract and L0 fact-card expansion

### Formal report vs. internal curator review
- [x] Draft PR #35 implements the conclusion-only assistant target and root-level internal_review separation.
- [x] Formal output fields: phenomenon_analysis, machine_result_interpretation, cause_localization, evidence_assessment, historical_experience_relevance, uncertainty, disposal_status/disposal_measures and follow_up_actions.
- [x] Curator prompts, alternative hypotheses, counterexamples and reviewer questions are explicitly not_for_sft.
- [x] NOT_RECORDED disposal requires an empty measure list; EXECUTED measures require resolvable source evidence; new follow-up suggestions remain separate.
- [x] Added L0 source_fact_card.schema.json and validator. L0 cards preserve source facts and missing-material flags; they always remain sft_eligible=false.
- [x] Latest PR #35 head b39205a7f0a0b5a90598ef2ed24944fc4da4de88: Ubuntu + Windows push CI PASS (43709303461) and PR CI PASS (43709309599).

### User-provided five cases
- [x] Created local L0 source fact cards from the user's original Word, preserving source statements and separating formal conclusion fields from internal reviewer questions.
- [x] Generated local Word and JSON files; neither user case payload has been committed to GitHub.
- [ ] User reviews case-level phenomenon analysis, fault-source/affected-object boundaries, source certainty and disposal wording.
- [ ] After review, determine which cases can be expanded with upstream ML results, diagnostic logs and spacecraft/mission context.

### Public literature expansion
- [x] Created 11 local L0 cards from public sources, with source class and evidence limits preserved.
- [x] Separated TROPICS ground qualification CRC/contact-resistance evidence from TROPICS Pathfinder in-orbit cross-interface short hypothesis.
- [x] Separated Lunar Orbiter III TWTA first-turn-on helix-current anomaly from temperature-sensitive power-monitor indication.
- [x] Separated NASA hydrazine injector blockage from catalyst poisoning within the same ground life-test event family.
- [x] Marked the ISEE/IUE report as an expert-system feasibility/knowledge source, not a real flight incident.
- [x] Classified the S-band TWTA 4 dB output-power case as a whole-spacecraft ground test, not an in-orbit failure.
- [ ] User reviews which literature-derived fact cards are appropriate for the experience library and which should be excluded.

### Data status
The five user cases and 11 literature cards are L0 source fact cards, not complete SFT packets. None has been promoted to Gold. Missing ML results, diagnostic logs, context and expert targets remain missing; no synthetic values were inserted into L0 records.

### Next
Continue literature-source verification and L0-to-L1 task design. Only after source fact cards are reviewed should explicitly labelled LITERATURE_DERIVED_SYNTHETIC upstream result/context packets be constructed for controlled SFT task testing. They must never be represented as real logs or real ML outputs.

### 2026-11-15 — Returned review package incorporated
- Received two revised Word files with 16 Word comments and a consolidated review memorandum.
- Confirmed the five user cases remain L0 source cards; all five causes remain source attributions pending case-level evidence. The user case payloads remain local and are not committed.
- “可自行恢复” is now represented as ambiguous source text, not a disposal action.
- Conditional protection branches, proposed actions and source-specific recommendations remain separate from executed historical measures.
- Public literature source records are now 12 L0 episode cards from 11 original literature entries. The two TROPICS payload outcomes have separate event_episode_id values under one shared event_family_id.
- ISEE/IUE is explicitly knowledge_source_not_event=true; it is excluded from real incident counts.
- NASA TM-100232 metadata separates report year 1987 from NTRS accession/cataloging year 1988; exact publication_date remains null.
- L0 schema now requires event class, event family/episode IDs, migration tier/rationale/constraints and missing-material inventory. All L0 cards remain sft_eligible=false.
- [Review decision record](docs/DGSI_L0_REVIEW_DECISIONS_20261115.md)
- [Public literature L0 JSON](examples/l0_public_literature_fact_cards_2026-11-15.json)

The review is AI-assisted and pending domain-expert confirmation. It does not approve Gold or establish missing ML results/logs/context.


### Final verification — 2026-11-15
- PR #35 latest head: `7c5a969048b7f7b09dcc1300dc1477769e9529fd`.
- [Push CI 43721453245](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43721453245): Ubuntu PASS, Windows PASS.
- [PR CI 43721448889](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43721448889): Ubuntu PASS, Windows PASS.
- 12 public-literature L0 cards are now in the PR branch. TROPICS A/B outcomes are separate episodes; NASA 22N injector/catalyst findings and Lunar Orbiter observations remain distinct episodes within their source families.
- L0 cards remain not SFT eligible. No Gold, model training or main-branch merge.


### 2026-11-15 — User-approved P4 direction and L1 implementation

User explicitly selected:
- Literature-derived synthetic tasks: **parallel** with a separate real-case/Gold track.
- Historical experience: **Context**, retrieved and included alongside current ML findings/logs/mission context.

Implementation:
- [x] Added strict L1 packet schema with REAL_CASE_CANDIDATE vs LITERATURE_DERIVED_SYNTHETIC.
- [x] Added L0 source-card binding and exact formal-target-to-Case binding.
- [x] Synthetic packets require field-level provenance for upstream ML result, logs, spacecraft context and operational context; synthetic run refs; recipe/version; assumptions; not-simulated list; and permanent non-Gold/non-real-flight flags.
- [x] Public knowledge-only sources cannot alone define synthetic incidents.
- [x] Historical Context validates equipment/subsystem/mission/operating-mode query scope, exact binding to Case history, no-hit semantics, event-family isolation, availability before analysis cutoff, confirmed-history as-of gate, and no upgrade of unresolved/rejected/partial/unknown cases.
- [x] Added 17 SYNTHETIC_TEST_ONLY adversarial tests and design documentation.
- [x] PR #39: https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/39 (Draft, stacked on PR #38).
- [x] Exact latest PR #39 head `692c36e0a360b8e2fd129ccb72ffa288ffb11a98`: Ubuntu 532/532 PASS, Windows 532/532 PASS — https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43724390941.

Current limitation: this is L1 structure/provenance/context validation, not yet a generated/reviewed L1 task collection or SFT effectiveness result. No real user-case payload, restricted log or raw telemetry committed; no Gold, fine-tuning or main merge.

Next:
1. Create a first small L1 literature-derived synthetic task set from reviewed public L0 cards, with explicit scenario provenance and independent scenario variants.
2. Add Context retrieval variants: no-hit, confirmed relevant, unresolved, rejected, incompatible hardware, conflicting history, post-cutoff and same-event-family.
3. Keep real-case L1 candidate path separate; await user/independent expert adjudication before Gold.
4. Design task-coverage and target-quality review before any controlled SFT experiment.

### 2026-11-15 — First L1 literature-derived synthetic task pilot

- [x] Added three L1 task packets bounded by reviewed public L0 cards:
  1. SEASAT slip-ring arc/short candidate;
  2. Lunar Orbiter III TWTA power-monitor measurement-chain ambiguity;
  3. TROPICS Pathfinder cross-interface common-cause short candidate.
- [x] Every synthetic packet has a synthetic upstream ML finding, synthetic timestamped logs, illustrative spacecraft/operational context, recipe/version, field-level generated-field provenance, scenario assumptions and not-simulated list.
- [x] All three use synthetic run IDs and explicit `LITERATURE_DERIVED_SYNTHETIC` track; all remain review-required, non-Gold and not real flight records.
- [x] First Context variants included: no-history retrieval and a rejected prior SEL hypothesis that is retained as REJECTED and cannot vote for the current root cause.
- [x] Added 3-packet fixture validation and evidence-reference integrity checks; initial CI found dangling L0 evidence IDs, fixed by binding targets to actual knowledge evidence IDs.
- [x] Added mixed history support so confirmed history is independently time-screened while rejected/unresolved history remains in its original status and can coexist for conflict-reconciliation tasks.
- [x] Added tests for conflicting confirmed/rejected history and incompatible hardware scope.
- [x] Added controlled SFT effectiveness protocol: Base, Generic Self-Instruct, DGSI synthetic, DGSI real Gold (when available), and DGSI + retrieved Context; real and synthetic holdouts reported separately.
- [x] 538 tests PASS on Ubuntu and Windows at code head `4ac4cb0fac23631941864c13bbe6717fa2ffd6bb`: https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43725174755.
- [ ] Verify both platforms at latest docs-updated head `cb3aab4debbdbe68fff8f9e9ce94cff0fbc5fa65` before opening/accepting PR #39.

The first three packets are L1 synthetic fixtures, not expert-approved training data. They do not contain real ML runs, real spacecraft logs or raw telemetry. The three task families are distinct and must remain isolated in future train/validation/test assignment.

Next: expand the Context variant matrix (no hit, confirmed relevant, unresolved, rejected, incompatible hardware, conflicting histories, post-cutoff, same event family), then build a small reviewed L1 set and a target-quality rubric. Do not start fine-tuning until the task packet set and evaluation holdout are reviewed.

### 2026-11-15 — L1 pilot and collection-level split audit

- [x] Created three source-bounded L1 literature-derived synthetic tasks: SEASAT slip-ring short candidate; Lunar Orbiter III power-monitor measurement-chain ambiguity; TROPICS Pathfinder cross-interface common-cause short candidate.
- [x] Each packet has explicit SYNTHETIC upstream finding/run ref, synthetic timestamped logs, illustrative configuration/mission context, field-level provenance, source L0 refs, assumptions and not-simulated list.
- [x] Formal targets contain conclusion-only report fields; curator prompts remain in Case internal_review.
- [x] First history Context variants: no hit and a rejected historical SEL hypothesis. Added tests for confirmed, unresolved, rejected, future, same-family, incompatible equipment and conflicting confirmed/rejected history.
- [x] Added L1 collection schema and collection audit. Enforces a single track per collection, packet count, unique task IDs, complete split assignment and event-family split isolation.
- [x] Pilot collection has 3 tasks, 3 source event families, REVIEW_REQUIRED status and no train/validation/test assignments yet.
- [x] Push CI at exact PR #40 head `e6f9e65663f369d6722c3908fa371ac42190a51b`: Ubuntu 543/543 PASS, Windows 543/543 PASS — https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43725715979.
- [x] Draft PR #39 implements L1 packet contracts: https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/39.
- [x] Draft PR #40 implements collection/split audit: https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/40.
- [x] Verify PR-triggered checks for #40 on the exact head: Ubuntu PASS, Windows PASS — https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43725828225.

No L1 packet has been promoted to Gold or approved for fine-tuning. Synthetic task counts remain separate from real-case counts.

### 2026-11-15 — History hardware applicability and expert target review

- [x] Each history Context item now distinguishes current query scope from the prior case's actual equipment scope and declares COMPATIBLE / INCOMPATIBLE / UNKNOWN.
- [x] INCOMPATIBLE history can only be retained as qualified contrast; target must state transfer limitations and cannot cite that case as supporting current root-cause evidence.
- [x] UNKNOWN compatibility requires explicit limitations; compatible/incompatible labels must agree with actual equipment scopes.
- [x] Added a 10-variant history Context coverage manifest and linked each scenario to executable synthetic tests.
- [x] Added weighted L1 target quality review (9 dimensions, 0–100) and automatic rejection gates. Score cannot override a rejection gate; review outcome cannot grant Gold or authorize training.
- [x] Added structured review schema, runtime validator and adversarial tests.
- [x] Latest push CI at `aacd92edf7eeac12f0476328f49d134d41bbf584`: Ubuntu 558/558 PASS, Windows 558/558 PASS — https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43727414285.
- [x] Draft PR #41: https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/41 (stacked on #40).
- [x] Verify PR-triggered CI for #41 on exact head: Ubuntu PASS, Windows PASS — https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43727528344.

Current L1 pilot remains three literature-derived synthetic packets, REVIEW_REQUIRED, non-Gold and not training-authorized. The context matrix consists of synthetic test variants, not additional real or Gold cases.

### 2026-11-15 — P4 independent L1 coverage and blinded-review metadata gate (Draft PR #42)
- [x] Added metadata-only L1 portfolio coverage: six task families, historical Context status buckets, event-family counts, and separate real-candidate versus literature-derived synthetic counts. No source case identifiers or diagnostic text in audit output.
- [x] Blocks formal split assignments on unreviewed collections and duplicate task IDs across collections.
- [x] Added dual anonymous review-scorecard validator for seven engineering dimensions (1–5), fixed finding codes, independent reviewer tokens and automatic secure-adjudication flag on disagreement. This cannot verify reviewer identity or approve Gold/training.
- [x] Added 12 SYNTHETIC_TEST_ONLY adversarial tests and [coverage/blind review rubric](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/blob/feat/l1-coverage-blind-review-20261115/docs/L1_TASK_COVERAGE_AND_BLIND_REVIEW.md).
- [x] Draft [PR #42](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/42), based on PR #40, exact head `2ee78727c0d6a5100a780b6b3d4507ab75f75d42`. [PR CI run 43727595149](https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43727595149): Ubuntu **555/555 PASS**, Windows **555/555 PASS**.
- Baseline: 3 L1 SYNTHETIC task packets / 3 distinct source event families / 2 diagnostic_synthesis + 1 conflict_reconciliation / 0 real Gold / 0 assigned splits. Other four task families still need coverage.
- PR #41 independently adds historical applicability and a nine-dimension expert quality rubric; reconcile the two review layers before adoption to avoid competing approval semantics. Neither PR is merged.
- Expert review is pending for first 3 L1 tasks and source cards. No training, Gold promotion or private data upload.


### 2026-11-15 — Expanded L1 pilot and independent blind-review gate

- [x] Expanded literature-derived synthetic L1 packets from 3 to 11 across 8 source event families.
- [x] Added TROPICS TVAC, separate payload A/B CRC episodes, Lunar Orbiter TWTA startup dual-candidate explanation, Cassini RWA drag, NASA 22 N injector plugging, NASA catalyst contamination, and S-band TWTA linearizer-LNA hydrogen poisoning.
- [x] Kept flight reports, ground tests and knowledge-only sources distinct. Ground-test tasks are explicitly ground-test context.
- [x] Related episodes remain grouped: TROPICS payload A/B, Lunar Orbiter power-monitor/startup, NASA injector/catalyst.
- [x] Corrected Lunar Orbiter startup target to preserve both source explanations without selecting an unsupported unique cause.
- [x] Added machine-readable 11-task/8-family coverage manifest and expert-review package v0.2.
- [x] Integrated history hardware applicability into the blind-review branch: COMPATIBLE / INCOMPATIBLE / UNKNOWN, with incompatible history barred from supporting current root cause.
- [x] Expanded independent blind-review scorecard to 10 dimensions. Requires two independent reviewers, fixed finding codes and secure adjudication; does not grant Gold/training.
- [x] PR #42 now contains aggregate coverage, two-reviewer blind review, hardware transfer checks and 11-packet pilot: https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/42.
- [x] Latest verified head `e157c9dda985d44365c22ba2a57aa89be20130e5`: Ubuntu 557/557 PASS, Windows 557/557 PASS — https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43729052218.

All 11 packets remain LITERATURE_DERIVED_SYNTHETIC, REVIEW_REQUIRED, non-Gold and not training-authorized. The next target is approximately 20 reviewed L1 tasks, but the remaining four task types need deliberate coverage, not paraphrase multiplication.

### 2026-11-15 — L1 history reuse and complete task-type coverage

- [x] Added public FUSE reaction-wheel drag L0 episode from the 2002 SPIE paper. Kept the 2000 pitch-axis drag episode separate from later 2001 wheel failures; vendor Kapton-liner explanation remains MOST_LIKELY.
- [x] Added FUSE↔Cassini historical Context task. Cassini prior outcome remains PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED; hardware compatibility UNKNOWN; its low-speed lubricant explanation and speed-management action cannot be transferred as FUSE root-cause evidence or current action.
- [x] Historical source refs now bind to public L0 cards; explicitly synthetic negative-history fixtures remain marked SYNTHETIC and require field-level provenance.
- [x] Added three task-type variants: TROPICS evidence_sufficiency, Cassini next_step_recommendation, and S-band TWTA handover_summary.
- [x] Pilot now contains 15 L1 synthetic packets across 9 source event families and covers all six declared Case task types.
- [x] Flight vs ground-test distinction, event-family grouping and no-Gold/no-training boundary remain enforced.
- [x] Latest head `67e9a020de9e8d6c993704113db1f1b8e9385614`: Ubuntu 559/559 PASS, Windows 559/559 PASS — push run https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43730903398; PR run https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43730907712.
- [x] Updated Draft PR #42: https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/pull/42.

All 15 remain literature-derived synthetic, REVIEW_REQUIRED, non-Gold and not training-authorized. No train/validation/test split assigned pending independent blind review.

### 2026-11-15 — Expert review package v0.3

- [x] Replaced the obsolete 11-task reviewer package with v0.3 covering all 15 L1 synthetic tasks, 9 source event families and 6 task types.
- [x] Added a dedicated FUSE–Cassini history-reuse review section explaining PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED status, UNKNOWN hardware compatibility and prohibited transfer of the Cassini speed-management action.
- [x] Included the 10-dimension two-reviewer blind-review form and automatic rejection criteria.
- [x] Local review artifact: `/mnt/data/DGSI_L1首批文献衍生合成任务_专家审核包_v0.3.docx` (delivered in the current ChatGPT conversation).


### 2026-11-16 — Complete receipt coverage and L0 domain-review binding

- [x] PR #44 adds `audit_l1_review_receipt_batch()`: one immutable receipt per task across all 15 L1 packets; missing, duplicate, unknown and cross-packet reused receipts are rejected.
- [x] PR #44 enforces source event/context alignment: ground-test source cards cannot silently become in-orbit scenarios and flight sources cannot be relabeled as ground-test/TVAC.
- [x] PR #44 push CI: Ubuntu 580/580 PASS, Windows 580/580 PASS — https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43737088830.
- [x] PR #44 PR CI: Ubuntu PASS, Windows PASS — https://github.com/clonetimer/Domain-Grounded-Self-Instruct/actions/runs/43737310944.
- [x] Corrected a governance ambiguity: the L0 collection root already states `AI_ASSISTED_REVIEW_PENDING_DOMAIN_EXPERT_CONFIRMATION`. Therefore the public source fact cards must not be described as domain-expert-reviewed.
- [x] Added per-card `domain_review_status` and `domain_review_evidence_sha256`. All 13 L0 cards are explicitly pending; none has a domain-review evidence digest.
- [x] L1 packet admission rejects domain-rejected L0 sources and blocks `APPROVED_FOR_L1_EXPERIMENT` while any referenced current or historical L0 fact remains pending or lacks a review-evidence digest.
- [x] L1 coverage and receipt-batch audits report source-review-state counts. The current 15-task pilot references 12 unique event source cards; all 12 are pending. The ISEE/IUE knowledge-only card is not used as an event source.

raw.body:
Backlog source: .ai/specs/2026-11-14-vereino-parity-facilities.md
Backlog id: E11

## 🎯 Change

Phase 5 (E08, #119) built the facility rules, rentals, requests, the log and the reports, but the screens stop short of the mockup, and several promises of the facilities spec were never built (`.ai/specs/2026-11-14-vereino-parity-facilities.md`, *Problem Statement*, verified against `a312199`). The owner compared the running application with the mockup and found it short "in every area, especially facilities" (D-031, *Why*). D-031 §4 makes the facility calendar the mockup's day axis, §1 turns the rules and records into tabbed pages, and D-029 puts every role but the administrator on the phone.

What the audit found:
- the panel calendar shows 2 of 6 entry kinds and never reads `GET /api/facilities/calendar`; the member calendar is a segment list booked in two steps;
- a rental cannot be opened or corrected, creates no charge, and its payment deadline is the constant 3 days;
- the attendant's pickers are empty and the rental dialog exists only in the panel, which D-029 takes away from the role;
- logs, incidents and club bookings can be created only from two member pages;
- renters and staff are not told about moves, cancellations and reschedule flags; an attendant's ban request reaches nobody;
- a one-off group event is not checked against the opening hours.

Who has it: the facility attendant; the club administrator; coaches and coordinators who book places; the person who maintains a place; the external renter.

## 📋 Scope

Expected outcome: README F-10 (the attendant's day and a rental by phone) runs entirely on a phone; J-005 (rental to payment) runs with a charge and the renter's e-mails; J-006 (a coach books a tournament) takes one tap from a free hour; J-R01…J-R08 of the spec pass.

Out of scope:
- the sidebar, the six facility menu items, the B-26/B-27 tab shells, menu count badges, the member "More" list, the attendant's landing page, the public header and the glossary (navigation spec, E09);
- registering `payments.chargeService`, the charge's payer and payee columns and the charge page (payments spec, E12);
- notices to guardians about a moved session and the coordinator's "needs reschedule" page (groups and activities spec, E10);
- the "add institution" link and other empty-picker hints (people life cycle spec, E13);
- editing a rental's amount, category or units; dragging on the axis; a week view; online payment by renters; accounts for regular renters; a ban appeal procedure.

## ✅ Done when

- every story below is closed;
- AC-R01…AC-R16 of the spec pass, with self-contained integration coverage (TEST-R01…TEST-R20) and `yarn verify` green;
- member and public pages are checked at 375 px, in both locales, in light and dark mode; panel pages in both locales and both modes.

## 📝 Spec

Design authority: `.ai/specs/2026-11-14-vereino-parity-facilities.md` (**Draft**, phases 1–16). It is an addendum to `.ai/specs/2026-10-27-vereino-facilities.md` (phase 5): it completes REQ-013…REQ-016, REQ-022…REQ-024 and REQ-029 and supersedes the rows listed in its table (recorded in `.ai/specs/changelog/2026-10-27-vereino-facilities/2026-11-14-parity-r.md`). Contract terms follow `.ai/specs/2026-10-20-vereino-club-management.md`. Sibling specs: navigation and naming (N, E09), payments (C, E12), groups and activities (A, E10).

Mockup screens: B-01, B-06, B-07, B-23…B-28, M-11, M-12, P-03…P-05 and flow F-10 (`docs/ux-concept/README.md`; `docs/ux-concept/mockups/app.ts`: `timeline`, `occupancy`, `dateChips`, `availabilityCard`, `slotModal`, `screenPlaces`, `screenPlace`, `screenFacilityToday`, `screenRentals`, `screenRequests`, `screenZones`, `screenLogs`, `screenOwnerReport`, `screenPublicPlaces`, `screenPublicPlace`, `screenVerify`).

## ⚠️ Open questions

- **Blocking — readiness:** the spec is **Draft**. No story is ready until the owner reviews it, confirms or overrides the autonomous defaults Q-R02…Q-R20 (two are flagged: Q-R09 departs from the mockup's one-click payment, Q-R18 needs a migration), and approves the items below (SDLC.md Definition of Ready).
- **Blocking for E11-S12 — migration:** the new table `facilities_rental_links`. Without approval the e-mails ship without the link and name the club's phone and the deadline.
- **Blocking — contract and behaviour changes (Ask First):** additive DI methods and fields in `club_core` (`placeOptions`, `searchInstitutions`, `facilityAgreement`) and `activities` (`placeSessions`); the consumer type of `payments.chargeService` and the 409 `rental_awaits_payment` on confirm; new `facilities` routes and response fields; the 409 `place_closed` on `POST /api/activities/events`; a past club booking for the club administrator; the facility terms inside `club_core_contracts.terms`. D-031 approves none of them.
- **Blocking for E11-S11:** E12-S01 (the charge service and its migration A) must land first.
- **Non-blocking — Q-R01:** "Potwierdź wpłatę" in one click and exact partial amounts in the owner report. Proposed default: no; the button opens the charge (DD-R09).
- **Non-blocking — Q-R21:** automatic expiry of unpaid rentals defaults to off.
- **Non-blocking — Q-R22:** coordinators see renters' names on the axis. Proposed default: names, as the mockup.
- **Non-blocking — move and amount:** the spec's non-goals say "a move re-quotes"; #221 records that a move to another place keeps the old amount and leaves it to the owner.

## 📋 Decisions in play

- D-031 §1 — the facility group has the mockup's six items; Zones and rates (B-26) and Log and incidents (B-27) are pages with tabs (product owner, 2026-11-14)
- D-031 §2 — names follow the mockup: place, request, incident, rental price list (the navigation spec's glossary)
- D-031 §4 — the facility calendar is the mockup's day axis; the week grid is dropped
- D-031 §6 — a session at a typed-in venue is on no facility calendar and is not checked against opening hours
- D-031, build order — N's phases 1–3 come before the other specs build UI; R's rental charge needs C's phase 1
- D-029 — every role but the administrator works from the phone
- D-030 — the administrator does the treasurer's work (records rental payments)
- D-028 — `payments` is optional for rentals; spec ids carry a letter
- DD-19 (charge seam), DD-41 (opening hours in `club_core`), DD-43 (occupancy lock), DD-44 (token handling), DD-46 (dispatch keys, `advanceWhere`) — facilities and club management specs
- R05 — 90-minute units, free cancellation up to 24 h
- Left as decided: #124 Q1 (public month view), #125 (request categories), #126 Q1 (attendant's no-show), #128 (maintenance page), #129 (rented-hours report), #121 (closure form as a page), #122 ("New rental" as a dialog); #221 holds the open E08-S02 follow-ups

## 📋 Stories
<!-- om-backlog: checklist, rewritten on every run -->
- [ ] #275 E11-S01 — Facilities pickers and lists read places from the module's own source, and the attendant's pickers are no longer empty
- [ ] #276 E11-S02 — An administrator sees one place's whole day on the hour axis of the facility calendar
- [ ] #277 E11-S03 — Staff tap a free hour and save a rental, a group event or a club booking from one slot dialog
- [ ] #278 E11-S04 — A coach or coordinator opens a place's day on the phone and books a free hour in one tap
- [ ] #279 E11-S05 — An administrator opens a rental from the list and corrects its contact, purpose, notes and renter
- [ ] #280 E11-S06 — An administrator decides a booking request from a card that shows every fact the decision needs
- [ ] #281 E11-S07 — An administrator works the zones, closures, price list, log, incidents and bans tabs and adds past records from the panel
- [ ] #282 E11-S08 — A facility attendant takes and manages rentals and asks for an entry ban, all on the phone
- [ ] #283 E11-S09 — A person who maintains a place sees, plans and completes their tasks on the phone
- [ ] #284 E11-S10 — An administrator sets the payment days and automatic expiry in the management agreement, and unpaid rentals are listed or expire
- [ ] #285 E11-S11 — A rental carries a charge payable to the place owner and is confirmed when the charge is paid
- [ ] #286 E11-S12 — A renter gets e-mails about their rental and cancels it through a link
- [ ] #287 E11-S13 — Staff are told when a closure or maintenance window flags their entry to be moved
- [ ] #288 E11-S14 — A one-off group event on a club place is refused outside the place's opening hours
- [ ] #289 E11-S15 — A guest sees the public places, calendar and request confirmation as the mockup shows them, inside the club's frame
- [ ] #290 E11-S16 — An administrator sees today's facility entries on the dashboard widget "Today at the facility"

raw.body:
Part 1 of 5 of #276. Its plan came to about 3900 changed lines, over the repo's limit, so it is built in 5 parts in this order. #276's original design is copied below under Original scope of #276, because a run cannot read GitHub. The Change list here is this part's spec: use the original scope only to resolve names and interfaces it mentions, and leave the other parts' work to them. It waits on #277 as well, since both rewrite state.py.

First stage of #276; prerequisite #273 is already landed at 9c8019c. Keep the repository working through state.py compatibility exports.

Create arete/store/db.py. Move FixtureConnection, connect_db, DB_LOCK and DB_THREAD from paths.py, retaining all confinement, sidecar, locking and isolated journaling behavior through paths helpers. Move the existing migrator, connection checking, db, reader, transaction, schema exceptions, schema constants, time mapping and compatibility checks from state.py without changing their behavior. Avoid package import cycles; migrations must validate owner metadata without importing aggregate implementations.

Move arete/migrations to arete/store/migrations. Preserve both numbered migration files and latest.txt byte for byte. Change only the loader as needed, including its diagnostic module name. Create the twelve aggregate modules with TABLES declarations using #276's mapping; additionally assign run_purges to runs and schema_meta/schema_migrations to db. Derive valid areas from actual public aggregate modules with TABLES, mapping foundation to db; reject outbox until its owner exists. Do not accept arbitrary helper files as migration areas.

Move foundation SQL out of dashboard.py and backup.py too: /api/meta's schema_meta read, inspection/counts, VACUUM INTO, migration-backup lookup and restore sequence operations become named store/db.py functions. The runs query used by backup.live_runs ultimately belongs to runs; temporarily retain its implementation behind a store function until the runs stage. Keep backup file operations and orchestration in backup.py, including raw pre-ledger inspection and recovery behavior. Every SQLite connection must be opened in db.py. Keep paths.py's filesystem helpers and path constants there.

Switch connection and migration callers, including CLI, serve, record schema stamps, backup, dashboard and test support, to the foundation module. Update trace instrumentation and mutable patches in tests/scripts/schema_ledger.py to target store.db. Update tests/test_storage.py historical migration discovery to follow renames and read each file at its original path in the adding commit; update copied-chain paths without weakening existing assertions.

Introduce the isolated subprocess probe tests/scripts/store_contract.py and its focused wrapper in tests/test_behavior.py. Initially cover ownership, unknown-area rejection and upgrade from 9c8019c, printing BEHAVIOR_RESULT JSON. Use all six isolated environment paths and replay.sample. Run through the allowed sandbox or behavior-check wrapper; no dependency installation or external setup is needed.

Do not alter numbered migration contents, create another migration, change the wire API, change security behavior or touch protected paths. Estimated non-move change: 900 lines.

## Original scope of #276

**Problem.** Lines are at main bd7d647. arete/state.py (2,308 lines, 219 functions) holds the DDL of all 43 tables and 17 indexes in one SCHEMA string (state.py:23-533), the order free MIGRATIONS list (state.py:534-590) that db() runs on every connect (state.py:592-606), and all table SQL but record.py's (record.py:54-131, 588-591). 44 of 91 modules import it. #273 moves SCHEMA and the ALTER list into migration 1 and gives each migration an `area`, but leaves the SQL, the shared fragments and prune in state.py, so `area` names no code and every table later issues add (`events_log`, `principals`, `tokens`, the inbox, outbox, secrets, refs) lands in the same file.

Shared fragments tie the aggregates together. FIRINGS (state.py:623-624) is both the filter of the runs list (state.py:627-642) and the predicate of prune, which deletes from feed, runs, queue, events and four incident tables in one transaction (state.py:906-922). OPEN_PR_RUN (state.py:13) is runs SQL inside the feedback query of feedback_due (state.py:1770-1778), and PAID_STEP and WHOLE_RUN (state.py:16-20) are steps and runs SQL. A branch that changes one aggregate edits the file every other branch edits. No row is wrong today; the cost grows with each new table.

**Change.**
- `arete/store/db.py`, area `foundation`: the connection (`FixtureConnection` and `connect_db` with its isolated mode, paths.py:131-180, move here and keep importing the path helpers from paths), `db()`, `reader()` and #273's `migrate()`, with what #273 puts in state.py beside it (`LATEST`, `NEEDED`, `NoDatabase`, the time column list). It owns `schema_meta` and `schema_migrations`, and later the tables of #281 (`events_log`, `principals`, `principal_logins`), #282 (`idempotency`) and #284 (`tokens`). It is the only module that opens arete.db. The writing transaction helper of the store lands with #277, not here; this change moves only the read and connect code and keeps `db()` as it is.
- #273's migrations folder moves from `arete/migrations/` to `arete/store/migrations/` with every file's bytes unchanged, so each applied row's `sha256` still matches. #273's upgrade test reads each migration at the path it had in the commit that added it (`git log --follow`), so it keeps passing after the move.
- One module per aggregate under `arete/store/`, each table in exactly one: `runs` (runs, steps, feed, record_pins, reports), `loops` (queue, events, loop_state, metrics, findings), `asks` (asks, messages), `approvals` (approvals, proposals, mined), `chats` (chats, chat_messages, chat_sessions), `tasks` (tasks, task_comments), `triage` (triage, triage_approvals), `sources` (seen, cursors, source_owners, passed_over), `incidents` (incidents, incident_notes, incident_repairs, incident_aliases, alerts), `devices` (vms, probes, holds), `insights` (usage, research, evals, feedback, verdicts, captures, capture_checks, capture_evidence), `push` (push_subscriptions). That is all 43 tables.
- Each module declares `TABLES`, a dict of each table it owns to its retention in a few words (`"kept"`, `"free command firings: 14 days"`), holds its vocabularies as constants (DECIDABLE and APPROVAL_NOTES to approvals, REFRESH_SCOPE to devices, USAGE_COLUMNS to insights, SEEN_AGAIN and CLOSED_AT to incidents), and exposes named functions that keep today's `connect=` argument (79 call sites in 14 modules pass `state.reader` or `state.db`, 35 of them in board.py).
- Shared fragments go to their owner: FIRINGS, OPEN_PR_RUN, WHOLE_RUN and PAID_STEP (until #312 replaces it with a stored paid amount) to `store/runs.py`.
- record.py keeps no SQL: the run insert, the step insert and cost update, `label_step`, `hold_ab`, `note`, `ask_stop`, `settle` and `runs_since` (record.py:54-131, 588-591) become `store/runs.py` functions that record.py calls. `settle` still writes its end feed line in the same transaction.
- A write across owners stays one transaction: the caller opens one `store.db.db()` connection and passes it to each owner's function that takes `c`. `commit_scan` (state.py:951-975) writes incidents, notes and aliases through `store/incidents.py` and its cursors through `store/sources.py` on that one connection. A read that joins another owner's table (`approvals` state.py:1101-1106, `vms_left_over` :1515, `open_asks` :2240-2245, `feedback_due`) stays one query in the module of the table it lists.
- Prune: `store/runs.py` (feed, then runs), `store/loops.py` (queue, events) and `store/incidents.py` (notes, incidents, aliases, repairs) each get one `prune(c, ...)` holding its own windows; `store.prune(days=14, keep_days=30)` calls them in today's order on one connection in one transaction, and `Server.prune` (serve.py:175-176, which passes `keep_days=self.cfg.oncall.keep_days`) calls it. It removes what `state.prune` removes at the base of this change, including any earlier fix that changed `state.prune` first (#246's backup before prune, #251's kept queue claims, #252's run folder retention).
- Migrations name their owner: `schema_migrations.area` is a store module name (`foundation` for store/db.py), and the runner's list of known areas is the store modules, so a migration that names an area with no module is refused. This replaces the fixed list of areas #273 ships. Every table a later change adds comes from a migration of the module that owns it; a change that adds a new aggregate adds its module.
- The move, one aggregate per PR: state.py first only passes store names through, so its 44 importers keep working. Callers then switch module by module, importing the store module (`from .store import runs`) and calling through it, so tests patch module attributes. state.py is deleted when nothing imports it.
- API: none; nothing changes on the wire.
- Contract: once the last importer moves, arete/state.py is deleted, record.py holds no SQL and no single prune deletes across owners. After this, #277's check of where writes happen reads `arete/store/`, and #314's reads "no store write outside serve".

**Done when:**
- New tests in tests/test_behavior.py run their cases in a subprocess with ARETE_CONFIG_DIR, ARETE_STATE_DIR, ARETE_LOG_DIR, ARETE_WORKTREES_DIR, TMPDIR and HOME under a TemporaryDirectory and config from `replay.sample`, as MinerRecordedRunTests.scratch does (tests/test_behavior.py:2705-2722), and print results as `BEHAVIOR_RESULT=` JSON.
- Test: an ast walk of every .py under arete/ outside arete/store/ finds no string literal or formatted string that starts with SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ALTER, DROP, PRAGMA, REPLACE or WITH followed by a space (case sensitive) and no call of `sqlite3.connect`, and arete/state.py does not exist. Today it fails on state.py, record.py and paths.py (the `PRAGMA journal_mode` at paths.py:178 and the connects at :142 and :175); the other modules already pass, and the `execute` methods of emits, push, sessions, verifiers and retrieval are not SQL.
- Test: with an empty state folder, `store.db.migrate()` builds arete.db; every table in sqlite_master but sqlite_sequence is a key of exactly one store module's `TABLES`, every `TABLES` key is a table in that file, and every `schema_migrations.area` is a store module name. A second case copies the migrations folder into the temporary folder, adds the next migration with area `outbox` and a matching latest.txt, and `migrate` on that copy is refused naming the file, since no `store/outbox.py` exists. Today #273's list of areas accepts `outbox`.
- Test: a DB built by `migrate` from the base commit's `arete/migrations/` (written into the temporary folder with `git show`) then migrated with `arete/store/migrations/` gets no sha256 refusal and no new `schema_migrations` row.
- Test: seed through record.start, record.settle and the store functions, backdated with an UPDATE as `made()` does (tests/test_behavior.py:2672-2678): free command loop firings started 30 and 1 days ago, each with a feed row; a paid command firing and a pipeline run started 30 days ago; queue rows enqueued 30 and 1 days ago, claimed and not; events 70 and 10 days old; an incident last seen 70 days ago with a note, an alias and a repair row; a dismissed incident closed 40 days ago with notes and evidence; an open incident with notes 20 and 1 days old. `store.prune()` leaves exactly the rows the test lists, which are the rows `state.prune()` leaves on the same seed at the base of this change. With `store.incidents.prune` patched to raise, `store.prune()` raises and no runs, feed, queue or events row is gone. `serve.Server().prune()` calls `store.prune` once with `keep_days=server.cfg.oncall.keep_days` (the patch at tests/test_process_limits.py:1029 moves to the store).
- The existing suites under tests/ pass, with test changes limited to import lines, the store names they call (`state.ticket_runs` becomes `runs.ticket_runs`, also inside the scripts tests run in a subprocess, such as `state.prune` at tests/test_oncall.py:2294 and :2296) and the four patch targets on state: tests/test_behavior.py:4360-4361, tests/test_process_limits.py:1029 and tests/test_oncall.py:531.

**Order.** Rebase on #273, whose migrator, ledger and migration files this moves into `arete/store/`. Best landed before #277, #281, #282 and #284 and the later tables, so the transaction helper, `events_log` and every later table are born in their owner's module; the writing transaction helper lands with #277, not here. Rebase on #246, #251 and #252 when they land first, since each changes `state.prune`. #314 extends the Contract check above to "no store write outside serve".

raw.title: [gap] Hosted spend breakdown: GET /v1/spend by day/model/agent and a dashboard Spend card that never counts unknown cost as $0
raw.body:
**User goal:** As a workspace owner or viewer, I want to open the dashboard and see spend for a chosen period broken down by day, model and agent, with unknown cost shown honestly, without downloading a CSV. Today the hosted dashboard shows one unlabelled "Synced receipt cost" total that sums every receipt in the retention window in the browser. It has no breakdown and no history view.

**GTM value:** "Which agent and which model burned the money, and on which day?" is the first question a paying buyer asks. Answering it makes the paid tiers' "Receipts shown for 90 days / 1 year" visible instead of CSV-only.

## Evidence (concrete code gap, HEAD `9010e33`)
- [`src/hosted/ui.js#L33`](https://github.com/persooninc/costcap/blob/9010e33/src/hosted/ui.js#L33): the only fleet-wide figure is a card labelled `Synced receipt cost`, with no period. The client `fleet()` sums every receipt it is sent (`total+=r.cost_usd`) and does no grouping.
- [`src/hosted/server.js#L398`](https://github.com/persooninc/costcap/blob/9010e33/src/hosted/server.js#L398) and `#L408`: `/v1/fleet` returns `receipts: visibleReceipts(s, u.orgId)`, every receipt in retention in one payload, and the browser does the sums.
- [`src/hosted/server.js#L126`](https://github.com/persooninc/costcap/blob/9010e33/src/hosted/server.js#L126): `spendSummary` gives only today, month and all-time totals. Nothing groups by model, day or agent, and `grep -rn "/v1/spend\|group_by\|breakdown" src/hosted` finds nothing.
- The promise:
  - [`src/billing/plans.js#L41`](https://github.com/persooninc/costcap/blob/9010e33/src/billing/plans.js#L41), `#L56`, `#L75`: "Receipts shown for 30 days / 90 days / 1 year" is what paid tiers add;
  - `docs/product-spec.md`: "Fleet view: every enrolled agent, its caps, live spend", and receipts carry "cost per model";
  - the hero copy: "Know the spend. Control the fleet."
- Competitor: LiteLLM groups spend by team, key and model in its spend reports: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/cost_tracking

## Scope
**In**
- `GET /v1/spend?since=&until=&group_by=day|model|agent`:
  - session auth, scoped to the org;
  - the period is clamped to the plan's receipt retention;
  - settled costs are applied (as `costedReceipt` does);
  - each bucket carries `usd_known`, `calls`, `unknown_count`, `blocked_count` and `cost_complete`.
- A pure `spendBreakdown()` module.
- A dashboard "Spend" card: a period picker (7d, 30d, this month), a per-day table or bars, and top models and top agents.
- The existing total card gets a period label.

**Out**
- Token and latency analytics.
- Forecasting.
- Removing `receipts` from the `/v1/fleet` payload (follow-up).
- Grouping by run.

## Acceptance criteria
1. On fixture receipts across 2 agents, 3 models and 3 UTC days, `GET /v1/spend` for each `group_by` returns buckets whose `usd_known` equals the hand-computed sums to 6 dp. Day buckets use UTC dates, and bucket totals add up to the response total.
2. Unknown cost:
   - a `cost_usd: null` receipt adds 1 to its bucket's `unknown_count` and sets `cost_complete: false`, never adding $0 to `usd_known`;
   - once settled, it counts at the settled value in its original day bucket, and `unknown_count` drops.
3. Access:
   - another org's receipts never appear;
   - no session returns `401`, and a viewer gets `200`;
   - an invalid `group_by`, `since` or `until` returns `400`.
4. With entitlements enforced, receipts older than the plan's retention are left out, and the response reports the clamped `since` with `retention_clamped: true`.
5. The dashboard "Spend" card renders day, model and agent rows from `/v1/spend` using `textContent` only (no HTML injection from model or agent names). It shows an "incomplete" badge on buckets with unknown cost, and refetches when the period changes.
6. Regression: `/v1/fleet`, `/v1/receipts.csv` and `/v1/evidence.json` responses are byte-identical for the same fixture store.

## Required tests (same commit)
- **Unit (`node:test`):**
  - a new `test/hosted-spend.test.js`: grouping math, unknown and settled handling, retention clamp, auth and `400`s, cross-org isolation;
  - `test/ui.test.js`: the spend card markup and `textContent` usage.
- **E2E (Playwright):** a new `e2e/spend.spec.js`. Sign in, sync receipts for 2 agents with mixed models (one unknown), assert the day, model and agent rows and the incomplete badge, switch the period, and confirm a viewer can see it. Existing `e2e/hosted.spec.js` and `test/hosted-server.test.js` stay green.

## Likely touched
- `src/hosted/server.js` (route)
- a new `src/hosted/spend.js`
- `src/hosted/ui.js` (card and client JS)
- `README.md` (hosted API), `docs/product-spec.md`
- the tests above

## Definition of done
- CI is green on `main` (test 20/22, e2e, gate, drift).
- The hosted app is deployed to app.costcap.dev.
- The docs are updated.
- The issue is closed with the commit sha.

opportunities.description:
## Live runtime evidence (2026-10-27)

A production Railway service **already exists**: `janavani-telegram-webhook` in project `janavani-telegram-bot`, sourcing `netzen-abm/janavani` branch `chore/eco

raw.title: [P0] Converge the existing Telegram webhook runtime into main and harden delivery
raw.body:
## Live runtime evidence (2026-10-27)

A production Railway service **already exists**: `janavani-telegram-webhook` in project `janavani-telegram-bot`, sourcing `netzen-abm/janavani` branch `chore/ecosystem-shared-capability-infrastructure`, deployed from commit `649d3f36e61ab0db7b9b368737c7ca1d8aa39694`. Its start command is `uvicorn src.web.telegram_webhook_app:app`, and Railway reports the latest deployment `SUCCESS`. Live proxy logs contain repeated Telegram-origin POSTs to `/telegram/webhook` returning `202` on October 26–27.

The webhook implementation already exists on that branch:
- `src/web/telegram_webhook_app.py`
- `src/web/telegram_webhook_config.py`
- `src/web/telegram_inbox_worker.py`
- `src/storage/repositories/postgres_telegram_inbox.py`
- `src/storage/repositories/postgres_telegram_inbox_worker.py`
- `tests/test_telegram_webhook.py`
- `tests/test_postgres_telegram_inbox.py`

It validates `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`, rejects malformed/oversized payloads, and encrypts updates in a PostgreSQL inbox before acknowledging them. The canonical bot builder is shared; on this branch, `src/bot_telegram.py:main()` fails closed with an explicit message rather than starting polling.

**Correction:** the first scan found no webhook in `main`, but there is an already-deployed implementation on the divergent shared-infrastructure branch. Do not build a second webhook. Converge this existing implementation selectively into current `main` and test it against the canonical runtime before switching any service source.

## Reliability issues found in live logs

- The webhook service is configured with `sleepApplication: true`. On 2026-10-27 around 03:32 UTC, the proxy recorded a Telegram webhook POST with upstream `connection refused` retries, then a `202` after roughly 12.2 seconds. Later requests returned `202` in about 2.5 seconds. Cold-start/wake behavior is therefore a delivery latency and retry-risk concern.
- On 2026-10-26 around 23:31 UTC, the webhook logs contained `psycopg.errors.ConnectionTimeout: connection timeout expired` while the inbox worker was claiming an update / shutting down. The worker has retry/backoff code, but the live connection timeout and shutdown sequence still need deterministic integration proof.
- The separate Railway service called `telegram-bot` currently runs `src.web.canonical_app:app` and is sleeping; it is not the webhook handler. Do not misidentify a green health check on that service as proof that Telegram request processing is healthy.
- `render.yaml` on `main` and `src/bot_telegram.py` on `main` still describe/permit a polling start path. That must be made fail-closed or pointed to the verified webhook only after the code is converged and deployment config is tested.

## Required sequence

1. Inspect the exact source commit running in Railway and compare its webhook/inbox files with current `main`. Extract only verified files and migrations—not the 638-commit branch history.
2. Prove webhook idempotency across duplicate `update_id`, encrypted inbox acceptance, restart, retry/dead-letter, lease reclaim, and worker shutdown. Ensure consequential bot actions cannot repeat on replay.
3. Add integration coverage for PostgreSQL timeout at startup/claim/shutdown and bounded recovery; do not log user text, secrets, DSNs, or exception messages that may contain payloads.
4. Resolve cold-start latency. If platform economics allow, keep the webhook service warm; if sleeping must remain enabled, verify Telegram timeout/retry behavior and ensure all retry paths are safe and observable.
5. Reconcile the main-branch startup/deployment declaration so polling cannot be started accidentally. Keep Telegram as an independently deployed service over shared capabilities.
6. Run CI and test against a fresh Railway preview/production candidate before changing the running source or promoting it.

## Acceptance

No Telegram polling runtime; one canonical webhook implementation; validated secret header; encrypted durable inbox; idempotent delivery; owner-linked identity for protected Case access; measured cold-start/recovery behavior; verified webhook request plus WebApp independence; CI and integration gates green.

## Additional privacy requirement for Telegram specifically

The Telegram Bot API is **not an end-to-end encrypted, local-only channel**. Telegram's official privacy policy explains that interacting with bots sends messages and some public account data to the bot developer; the Bot API does not operate inside Telegram Secret Chats. Therefore:

- Before asking citizens to describe an issue in bot chat, show a concise notice that Telegram and the Janavani bot service process the messages necessary to provide the service.
- Do not describe bot chat as E2E encrypted, private-from-Telegram, or local-first.
- Do not request identity documents, medical/legal-sensitive details, or original evidence as routine bot inputs. Where a workflow needs sensitive content, route the citizen to a locally controlled WebApp / Mini App path where feasible and explain the data boundary before they proceed.
- Strip unnecessary bot metadata and message content from logs. Keep the webhook inbox encrypted, retention bounded and verified; clear payloads after processing/expiry according to policy.
- A user's choice to use Telegram is not consent to broader collection, cross-surface replication, AI processing, or public disclosure. Require separate, specific choices for those operations.

Official source: Telegram Privacy Policy (https://telegram.org/privacy) and Telegram bot FAQ (https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq#what-messages-will-my-bot-get).
